details.publicNotes:
A quantum hummer is a colorful, musical bird whose wings beat fast enough to distort spatial probability. This causes the bird to appear in multiple places simultaneously as a swarm consisting only of itself. The creature uses this ability to evade predators and communicate with members of its kind through song. Direct, precise observation of a quantum hummer collapses its spatial probability, thwarting the bird's superposition and leaving it vulnerable.

Though their heads have dark spots that mimic eyes, quantum hummers are blind and rely on their swarming songs and keen hearing to communicate and navigate their environment. The exchange of songs between quantum hummers builds the foundation of their social structure, and they work diligently to perfect a song to elevate their status and attract mates.

Quantum hummers are drawn to pleasing sounds and melodies and enjoy collecting musical items like small wind chimes and bells and storing them in dangling nests to accompany their songs. Quality musical performances can easily draw the attention of a quantum hummer, who might follow the musician on their journey or attempt to trade an item from their collection for the musician's instrument.

Quantum Tunneling

Sages speculate that, since the act of observing a quantum hummer can change its state from a swarm to an individual, an unobserved quantum hummer is both a swarm and an individual. To test this theory, one enterprising scholar tried putting a quantum hummer in a sealed birdhouse to see whether it would eat enough birdseed for a single bird or an entire swarm. When they opened the house, they found a surprising result: no birdseed, no bird, and a hole to another dimension pecked through the back of the structure.

description.value: A quantum hummer can use their hearing as a precise sense at the listed range.

Requirements The quantum hummer is not @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized}, and there are at least three unoccupied squares adjacent to the quantum hummer

Effect The quantum hummer moves rapidly to distort space and appear in multiple adjacent spaces, becoming @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]. While they distort their position in this way, they become a Large swarm, with immunity to the @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei], @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}, and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained} conditions as well as weakness 5 to area damage and splash damage. The bird remains in this state until they are immobilized or @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious}, or until their precise location is observed, typically through an effect that negates invisibility or a critically successful Perception check to @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek} them. A quantum hummer can Dismiss Superposition.

Trigger The quantum hummer hears a Swarming Song from another quantum hummer within 40 feet

Effect The quantum hummer enters a Superposition. If the quantum hummers is already in a Superposition, they instead perform a Swarming Song.

Requirements The quantum hummer exists in a Superposition

Effect Each enemy in the swarm's space takes @Damage[3d6[sonic]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:24|basic] save). A creature that fails its save against Swarming Song becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.9PR9y0bi4JPKnHPR]{Deafened} for 1 round. In addition to the typical @Check[flat|dc:5] to perform actions with the auditory trait while deafened, creatures that are deafened from Swarming Song must succeed at @Check[flat|dc:5] to perform concentrate actions.

The quantum nature of the quantum hummer's body attack allows them to Strike from multiple places at once. If the quantum hummer is in a place where teleportation effects are suppressed, their reach decreases to 0 feet, the damage of their quantum beak is reduced to 2d6, the damage of their quantum wing is reduced to 2d4, and their Strikes lose the teleportation trait.
